comments.body:
**History expiry**

Followup from last ACDE: 

- It seems there is consensus on using the CL block retention window for history expiry. I'd be keen to either update 4444 or have some informational EIP so that this is documented

- [Nethermind PR](https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/pull/12808) to change it is here. Is there an update from other clients?

- Could clients and other entities also update [history endpoints](https://eth-clients.github.io/history-endpoints/) so we have a list of folks who are providing history? [Nethermind and PandaOps added here](https://github.com/eth-clients/history-endpoints/pull/17)

**PQ**

The current beacon deposit contract (and a few others) are not suitable for PQ. 

There are two high level strategies to supporting the new PQ functionality: deploy a new deposit contract, modify the old deposit contract via an irregular state transition (adding a new function for PQ).

I would like to get the opinions on how folks think we should move forward.

Also curious to know why we are not using a precompile/tx/opcode for deposits, was this a part of the design space?

I would like to do a quick demo of the proposed API for the EIP-8304 trustless log index (which answers log search queries with efficient proofs and also offers advanced features compared to the json rpc log query). This should be useful for evaluating the current maturity level of the project and the merits of the eip before the hegota eip ranking deadline.

To simplify implementation, I am withdrawing EIP-7686, EIP-7971, EIP-7973 and EIP-7923 (PFId) from the PFI list. I am currently left with the following three PFI EIPs:
EIP-7609: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/11893
EIP-8058: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/11894
EIP-8360: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12074
I am not withdrawing EIP-7923 and will champion this EIP.

hi @Helkomine i'll add them to the agenda - each of these will still need someone to speak for them. if no one can speak for them on this Thursday's call, they'll be dropped from PFI and will need to be re-proposed for i-star
What I mean is, since the EIP has already been proposed, I won't propose it again.

Requesting a couple of minutes on the agenda for state-gas refills for same-tx created-and-destroyed accounts (EIP-8037)

Kind of related to @Helkomine proposal tho I advocate to fix this in 8037 instead of introducing new features last minute. Also, has been already implemented for failed transactions.

More context: https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/1540737956929736766
And https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/eip-8037-state-creation-gas-cost-increase/25694/46?u=milonite_2

Tldr:
As long as same-tx selfdestruct stays in the EVM (and there’s no alternative for ephemeral contracts), the account charge should be refilled when no state was created.
Otherwise the incentive is backwards. Leaving the account in state ends up cheaper than destroying it. And there's no real alternative for the contracts and applications that need this and in practice the charge just moves these flows to L2
I want to signal that I see there is no champion (currently?) for [EIP-4758](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-4758) (correct me if I'm wrong), I will champion this EIP.
I don't want that EIP to be implemented so soon because it would prevent temporary accounts.

Same, @jochem-brouwer what's the reason to championing that EIP (Stagnant since 2022) without an alternative for temporary account and ephimeral contracts? 
Moves an important use case to Layer-2 only. 
4758 should be implemented alongside an alternative. I'm in favor of deprecating selfdestruct, but there must be an alternative for ephimeral contracts.
Need some eyes on [eth_simulateV1 issues](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/issues/868) for Glamsterdam
sharing https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12249 <- specs by @chfast for 8037 fix. This would be for Glamsterdam, not Hegota
